GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM.

(GENERAL ENGLISH)

SECTION - A (Conventional Type) (40 Marks)
This section should be answered only on the Answer Sheet provided.
Marks for each question is indicated against it.
1. Write an essay on any one of the given topics.
(10)
- Artificial Intelligence and Healthcare – pros and cons
- Importance of Psychology and Mental Health lessons
- Scope and Potential of Health Tourism in Mizoram
2. Write a précis of the following passage in about 1/3 of its original length, giving it suitable title. (10)
Trees give shade for the benefit of others, and while they themselves must stand directly in the
sun and endure the scorching heat of the day, they continue to produce the fruit by which others
profit. They do not hoard their gifts, nor do they complain of the weather. The character of good and
noble men is exactly like that of these trees. We must ask ourselves: what is the use of this perishable
body, which is destined to decay, if no use of it is made for the lasting benefit of mankind? A life lived
only for the self is a life wasted.
Consider the natural world and the lessons it yields. Take sandalwood- the more it is rubbed
against a hard surface, the more of its sweet scent does it yield to the air. Consider the sugarcane—
the more it is peeled, crushed, and cut into small pieces, the more delicious juice does it produce for
the thirsty. Look at gold—the more it is burnt in the crucible of the forge, the more brightly and purely
does it shine.
The men who are truly noble at heart do not lose these divine qualities even in the process of
losing their very lives. To them, the external world is secondary. What does it matter whether common
men praise them or not? What difference does it make whether great riches abide with them or
whether they live in poverty? What does it signify whether they die at this very moment or whether
their lives are prolonged for many years?
Happen what may, those who tread in the right path of righteousness will not set foot in any
other, for their integrity is absolute. Life itself is unprofitable and hollow to a man who does not live
for the service of others. To live for the mere sake of living one’s own life is to live the base life of
dogs and cows, driven only by instinct. Those who lay down their lives, even for the sake of a friend,
or even for the sake of a complete stranger, will assuredly dwell forever in a world of eternal bliss.

- 2 -
3. During the past year there were several cases of death in your village due to the absence of qualified
doctors in the Primary Health Centre. There was also an outbreak of cholera and the medical personnel
were insufficient to cope with the crisis. Write a letter to the Minister, Health and Family Welfare
Department, requesting for at least two qualified doctors to be posted in your village. Sign yourself as
ABC of XXX, YZ District
(10)
4. Read the following passage and answer the question given below:
Many people believe that science and religion are contrary to each other. But this notion is
wrong. As a matter of fact, both are complementary to each other. The aim of both these institutions
is to explain different aspects of life, universe and human existence. There is no doubt that the methods
of science and religion are different. The method of science is observation, experimentation and
experience. Science takes its recourse to progressive march towards perfection; the rules of religion
are faith, intuition and spoken word of the enlightened; in general, while science is inclined towards
reason and rationality, spiritualism is the essence of religion.
 In earlier times when man appeared on earth, he was over-awed at the sight of violent and
powerful aspects of nature. In certain cases, the usefulness of different natural objects of nature
overwhelmed man. Thus began the worship of forces of nature-fire, the sun, the rivers, the rocks, the
trees, the snakes, etc. The holy scriptures were written by those who had developed harmony between
external nature and their inner self. Their object was to ennoble, elevate and liberate the human spirit
and mind. But the priestly class took upon itself the monopoly of scriptural knowledge and interpretation
to its own advantage. Thus the entire human race was in chains. Truth was flouted and progressive,
liberal and truthful ideas or ideas expressing doubt and skepticism were suppressed and their holders
punished. It was in these trying circumstances, the science emerged as a saviour of mankind. But its
path was not smooth and safe. The scientists and free thinkers were tortured. This was the fate of
Copernicus, Galileo, Bruno and others. But by and by science gain ground.
(a) Why does man worship the force of nature?
(2)
(b) Why is it said in the passage that ‘science emerged as a saviour of mankind’?
(2)
(c) How does the passage distinguish between the methods used by science and those used by
religion?
(2)
(d) Based on the text, what kind of treatment did early scientists like Galileo and Bruno face, and
why?
(2)
(e) In what way does the author argue against the notion that science and religion are contrary to
one another?
(2)

- 3 -
SECTION - B  (Multiple Choice questions) (60 Marks)
All questions carry equal mark of 1 .  Attempt all questions.
This section should be answered only on the OMR Response Sheet provided.
Notes regarding Negative Marking :
(i) There will be penalty (negative marking) for every wrong answer given by a candidate in the
MCQ type questions.
(ii) For each question for which a wrong answer has been given by the candidate, one third of the
marks assigned to that question will be deducted as penalty.
(iii) If a candidate gives more than one answer to one question, it will be treated as wrong answer
even if one of the given answers happens to be correct and there will be same penalty as
above for that question.
(iv) If any questions is left blank i.e. no answer is given by the candidate, there will be no penalty
for that question.
